activity_context.topic_title: Row and Column Operations on Determinants

feedback.problem: Suppose $C$ is a $4\times 4$ matrix and $det(C)=5.$ What is the value of $det(-3C)?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Multiplying a $n\times n$ matrix by a scalar $k$ is equivalent to multiplying each row by $k,$ and this occurs $n$ times. This leads to the result

$$
\begin{aligned}det(k\cdot C)={k}^{n}\cdot det(C).\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we have $k=-3$ and $n=4.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}det(3C) & =(-3)^{4}\cdot det(C) \\  & =81\cdot 5 \\  & =405.\end{aligned}
$$
